title: When a Nightly Video Factory Goes Silent for 2 Days | vitalii.no
description:
How a self-hosted video pipeline learned to reset its own memory before every run — after a silent two-night outage that no log flagged as a failure.

On September 5th the factory's own AI agent session quietly grew past 47.5 MB. Every wake after that failed on a "prompt too long" error, produced zero clips, and the task tracker still marked each run as completed. Nothing looked broken from the outside — it just went quiet for two days.

A Python routine now rotates the agent's session context before every single wave instead of waiting for a size threshold: a measurement across real runs showed the gap between compactions is normally under 1 MB, so any bigger threshold was already too late in disguise. The nightly job also moved from one shared task covering the whole night to one task per clip with its own 45-minute timeout, so a single feature failing can't take the rest of the batch down. A new watchdog process watches for silence rather than size, giving a failed night exactly one retry the next day, with a Telegram note explaining what happened.

The pattern that caused the outage — a session ballooning past 47.5 megabytes before it stopped producing anything — is exactly what the new rotation now catches before it can happen again.
